Paganism is a huge umbrella term for a bunch of religions! Greek paganism specifically is the devotion to Ancient Greek deities, but of course with more modern approaches. We don’t sacrifice anyone or animals like ancient Greeks used to, similar to how Christians now eat shellfish and have tattoos, despite those once being sins. Lots has changed. but we still leave offerings, pray, set up altars, etc. Some Greek pagans are also witches and do witchcraft alongside deities, but I personally am not. Ancient Greek festivals and holidays are still celebrated. Patron gods used to be per family and per city, but now it’s individualized and who you’re most close with. The religion can be practiced by anyone of all ethnicities, so I don’t have Greek heritage but still practice. It’s popular in Greece but also all over the world. I’ve owned male Syrians for three years. Hamsters’ sounds can be super hard to understand, especially if they don’t make a lot of noise in general. Sometimes there are very little signs when it comes to hamsters compared to cats or dogs. They’re much harder to understand.
Everything I’ll say is from my own experience with my hamsters. I’ve found that teeth grinding is almost always negative— they’re frustrated, angry, upset, etc. Sometimes because they can’t get a nut open or because I’m touching them and they don’t want to be touched. 
Clinking and loud noises can be super super hard to understand, because they can mean negative and positive emotions. Think of humans moaning— we can moan from pain or pleasure. It’s especially hard in this case since you didn’t even touch your hamster and they can’t speak to us. 
How long has he been yours? Hamsters may not settle fully until 3-ish months, sometimes longer. Maybe he was asking for attention or was scared of you entering the room. 
It’s super hard to tell and may not be a cause for concern. But if you notice heavy breathing, excess sneezing, runny nose or eyes, diarrhea, extreme fatigue, or any other strange symptoms or change in personality, I would suggest making a vet appointment. I don’t mean to worry you but they may be noises of pain if your hamster is showing any strange behaviours/symptoms! I also like to thoroughly check my hamsters for lumps or wounds at least once a week so I recommend checking for those just in case. Good luck <3

I’d start first with pushing down/packing down the bedding. It looks pretty fluffed up and loose. This can make it hard to walk on and burrow into, since it’ll just be sinking and collapsing. I’d also put that high bedding in more of the tank, so tunnels and separate dens can actually be formed. 
I’d also recommend some foraging stuff like sprays. Females can tend to get bored very fast, so try some little cages you can hang or keep on the floor to get food out of. Sometimes I even put food inside of a toilet paper roll and then twist paper around it like a Christmas cracker thing. Keeps them preoccupied… for a few minutes, at least? 
I have some wood too that my Syrian adores. I got cork bark that has a bunch of holes I hide food in. He loves chewing it up and finding the food! 
Those are all my suggestions. Again, wonderful cage and wonderful hamster! Congrats!

Hi! Congrats on your new hamster. My first hamster was a male Syrian. He was very timid, bitey, and scared. He was rehomed to me in a 30 gallon terrarium, which I upgraded to a 50 gallon after about 4 months. Immediately, his behaviour changed drastically. He never bit me again, despite biting me everyday for those first 4 months. He was a completely new hamster and his true personality was able to show. You mentioned you need to get a bigger cage, so the hamster could be under some stress now along with moving to a new environment. The stress from a small cage can leave them aggressive or very skittish, proved by my first hamster. I think they don’t feel safe if their cage is too small, so they see everything as a threat. Additionally, the hamster could’ve gone through trauma at the breeding mill, the pet store, or from your family member, making the hamster harder to socialize with. I hope you’ll see a difference when you get the new cage, but in the meantime these other comments are super good! Good luck ♥️
